text:
Echo State Networks (ESNs) are a type of recurrent neural network used for processing time-series data. They consist of a large, fixed-size, randomly connected hidden layer called the reservoir, which processes the input data. The weights of the reservoir are typically fixed, and only the output weights are trained. Training involves adjusting the output weights to map the reservoir's activations to the desired output. Reservoirs are often trained using random connectivity and spectral radius tuning to ensure they have the right level of excitability.
